strategyReview: Live performance leans on weekend funding reversion (71% win rate, +$1.26) and one‑touch NO edge (4/4 live wins, +$0.74). Absolute funding long/short signals are marginal or losing, and the old BTC PM‑IV expansion thesis with static thresholds is failing; its regime‑relative successor shows promise. Shadow‑mined families – gold one‑touch heatmap, cross‑asset IV compression, and loose weekend funding triggers on CBRS/AAPL/MU – repeatedly miss because they assume fast mean reversion without trend confirmation or true weekend context.

failureClusters.theme: Static Funding Mean‑Reversion Without Trend Filter
failureClusters.evidence: FUNDING_EXTREME_LONG is live but produces 44% win rate and -0.49% average PnL; FUNDING_EXTREME_SHORT barely breaks even. The disabled LLM_HYPOTHESIS family also lost money by forcing long/short bets on non‑trend‑filtered data.
failureClusters.recommendation: Shift from absolute funding thresholds to asset‑specific, trend‑confirmed signals; limit positions to conditions where funding is extreme relative to its recent distribution and aligned with macro trend.

failureClusters.evidence: The only tested variant H‑534 went 0/20 predicting a >2% spot decline when gold’s underlying‑cap edge exceeded 10 pts. Every resolution saw gold flat or rallying, with the largest loss at +5.37%.
failureClusters.recommendation: Do not trade the edge alone; require a bearish trend filter (spot below 24h SMA) or confirm with PM IV rich condition, otherwise the edge may just reflect retail premium, not directional information.

failureClusters.theme: Cross‑Asset IV Compression / HYPE Momentum Confirmation
failureClusters.evidence: Nine different variants all lost, never achieving the required >2% BTC upside. The HYPE risk‑on criteria added noise; BTC moved sideways or down while HYPE held steady.
failureClusters.recommendation: De‑couple the HYPE condition and test BTC momentum alone with volatility expansion, or redesign the confirmation with a different leading indicator (e.g., options flow).

failureClusters.evidence: Signals entered at funding <‑10% without a weekend‑day filter suffered repeated losses when funding failed to normalize (e.g., CBRS from -8% to -162%). Many winning shadows actually required true weekend context.
failureClusters.recommendation: Refine each shadow‑mined setup by adding a {day_of_week: in [sat, sun]} condition and raising the funding‑extremity threshold to <‑20% or bottom 5th percentile of its 7d range.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑534: Add a bearish trend filter to the gold one‑touch NO edge short. Only sell‑YES when the underlying‑cap edge is large AND gold spot is below its 24h SMA, confirming that the edge aligns with a weak trend. This should prevent shorting into a persistent rally.
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot will decline >2% within 5 days when a large underlying‑cap edge on upside one‑touch NO contracts occurs while spot is below its 24‑h moving average.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑539: Restrict CBRS weekend funding reversion to true weekends and require extreme funding (<‑20% annualized). This addresses the failure where non‑weekend and mildly negative funding triggers did not normalize.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS perp price will rise >2% within 2 days when funding is deeply negative on a Saturday or Sunday.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑537: Apply weekend‑only filter and deeper funding‑extremity threshold (<‑20%) to AAPL funding reversion. Previous losses came from weekday triggers where funding did not revert quickly.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL spot will gain >2% within 2 days when funding is extremely negative on a weekend day.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑535: Limit MU weekend funding reversion to weekends and raise the funding threshold to <‑20%. Losses occurred when funding was only moderately negative on weekdays and failed to mean‑revert.
newHypotheses.prediction: MU spot will increase >2% within 2 days when funding is severely negative on a Saturday or Sunday.

newHypotheses.description: Fade dumb money highs: sell‑YES on upside one‑touch NO contracts when smart wallets are net short (stance ≤ -1) and a sell‑YES edge ≥2 pts exists. The FIND‑0020 study shows smart‑flow disagreement predicts reversion.
newHypotheses.prediction: The underlying asset spot price will decline >2% within 7 days as smart‑money selling YES precedes a spot correction.

newHypotheses.description: GOLD extreme low put/call ratio short signal. When the 7‑day percentile of gold_gld_pc_ratio falls to the bottom 10%, the contrarian short hypothesis wins 100% in the shadow cluster (FIND‑0053).
newHypotheses.prediction: GOLD spot will decline >2% within 5 days following an extreme drop in put/call ratio (extreme call buying).

newHypotheses.description: Rich PM IV touch NO fade: when Polymarket IV exceeds the listed‑option IV by ≥10 vol points on an upside one‑touch contract with a positive sell‑YES edge, sell‑YES to short the underlying. The FIND‑0021 cluster shows 90% win rate and +0.98 sum PnL.
newHypotheses.prediction: The spot price of the underlying asset will fall >2% within 5 days as the rich PM IV premium compresses.

newHypotheses.description: BTC‑specific one‑touch NO edge with moderate strength: sell‑YES on BTC upside touch contracts when the sell‑YES edge is between 3 and 8 pts. The FIND‑0043 cluster returned 75% win rate, +1.97 total PnL in shadow.
newHypotheses.prediction: BTC spot will decline >2% within 5 days when a moderately strong sell‑YES edge appears on upside one‑touch NO contracts.

newHypotheses.description: Broad one‑touch NO edge across all assets with above‑strike direction and edge 3‑8 pts. The FIND‑0030 shadow has 55% win rate but positive sum PnL after incorporating tight spread constraints (default).
newHypotheses.prediction: The underlying asset will decline >2% within 5 days when a moderate NO edge exists on an upside touch contract expiring within 30 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑534 lost all 20 tests. The large underlying‑cap edge on gold NO contracts did not predict spot declines; gold rallied sharply on the largest moves. The edge reflected market pricing of tail risk, not directional flow, making the signal intrinsically negative when trend is positive.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying‑cap edge on gold upside one‑touch NO contracts reliably predicts a >2% spot decline within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑539 yielded mixed results (47% win) because CBRS funding below -10% included many weekday instances where funding failed to normalize. The assumption that any deeply negative funding represents a weekend overshoot is false; many losing cases deepened further or stagnated.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative weekend CBRS funding rapidly normalizes, causing a >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑537 recorded 43% wins. Non‑weekend triggers dominated the losses, as AAPL funding often reversed slower than the 2‑day window. The thesis that extreme negative AAPL funding alone leads to spot recovery is invalid without the weekend‑only context that made shadows profitable.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative AAPL funding rapidly normalizes and leads to a >2% spot gain without requiring a true tail‑event overshoot.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑535's 44% win rate shows that MU funding < -10% on any day is not a reliable long signal. The winning shadows almost always occurred on weekends; losses happened when funding was negative on weekdays and continued to drift.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative MU funding (< -10%) outside of true weekend hours rapidly normalizes and produces >2% spot gain.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑001's absolute IV thresholds (PM IV <46, opt IV >49) captured periods of low volatility compression where spot moved less than 2%. The regime‑relative successor H‑523 (using bottom‑20% compression) is performing much better (67% win), confirming that static levels are not predictive.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC PM IV below 46 while options IV remains high guarantees a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days regardless of trend context.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All 2 tests from H‑108 failed to reach the >2% BTC target. The combination of BTC and HYPE both above their short‑term SMAs with stable OI did not precede further rally; instead, BTC ranged or dipped.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC above short‑term trend with HYPE spot above SMA and OI stable confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3‑7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: H‑523 (BTC PM IV regime‑relative compression) is working: 67% win rate (4/6) in recent tests, successfully capturing large absolute moves when PM IV is in the bottom 20th percentile. This validates regime‑relative over static thresholds and should become the primary BTC vol expansion signal.

H‑551 (OIL one‑touch NO edge, 80% win) is showing strong live validation. The signal’s use of edge‑only condition on OIL upside touch contracts is proving robust; worth considering for promotion once the shadow test bar is met.

journalEntry: Tonight’s research focused on killing failing variants and capturing the highest‑confidence FIND opportunities. Static funding and PM‑IV thesis families are now clearly underperforming; the regime‑relative approach and edge‑based one‑touch signals are where live profitability lies. Weekend funding refinements must incorporate explicit {day_of_week} filters to avoid weekday noise. We added seven new hypotheses from top‑ranked FINDs and four structural refinements to the struggling weekend funding shadows. The learnable parameter set is stable; no immediate risk adjustments needed until the live open PnL ratio shifts.
